title: Paradigmes des courbes algébriques (version provisoire) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from p.1): X is a connected, non-empty scheme over Q̄ ⊂ C. 𝒢_X is the group of automorphisms of X as an absolute scheme, that is, Q̄-semilinear automorphisms. It sits in 1 → G_X = Aut(X/Q̄) → 𝒢_X → Γ = Gal(Q̄/Q). Choose a universal (pro-étale) covering X̃ → X. Let ℰ_X be the group of absolute automorphisms of X̃ that lift some element of 𝒢_X. (The earlier notation 'Aut(X̃/X)' should be read as 'automorphisms of the pair (X̃, X)'; otherwise (6) would make no sense.)

The exact sequence (6), 1 → π1(X) = Aut(X̃/X) → ℰ_X → 𝒢_X → 1:
- Surjectivity holds because for u ∈ 𝒢_X the pullback u*X̃ is again a universal cover, hence isomorphic to X̃, so u lifts.
- The kernel is the deck group, i.e. the geometric étale π1.
- Composing with 𝒢_X → Γ gives a model-free 'arithmetic fundamental group' of X. It also incorporates the geometric automorphisms of X, without choosing a field of definition.

The point ξ ∈ X(Q̄), (7): let 𝒢_X(ξ) be its stabiliser in 𝒢_X. The NB says that if the geometric group G_X is finite, then 𝒢_X is profinite and 𝒢_X(ξ) is open; this uses the fact that ξ is defined over a number field.

Partial splitting (8): take X̃ pointed by ξ̃ over ξ. Each g ∈ 𝒢_X(ξ) has a unique lift fixing ξ̃, because π1 acts simply transitively on the fibre. This gives a homomorphism s_ξ: 𝒢_X(ξ) → ℰ_X splitting (6) over the stabiliser. For an unpointed X̃, s_ξ is only defined up to inner automorphisms coming from π1(X).

Purpose (continued on p.3): restrict along a germ of lift Γ' → 𝒢_X on small open Γ' ⊂ Γ, which exists when X is of finite type. For Γ' small enough it fixes ξ, which yields φ_ξ: Γ' → ℰ_X, well defined up to π1-conjugacy. This is the standard 'rational point ↦ conjugacy class of Galois section' map underlying the section conjecture (letter to Faltings, 1983). Here it is formulated equivariantly with respect to the full absolute automorphism group, in preparation for 'paradigms' of curves (moduli-free, field-of-moduli setting).
errors: Notation on p.1, (5) 'ℰ_X = Aut(X̃/X)' clashes with (6), where Aut(X̃/X) = π1(X) is the kernel. ℰ_X must be the group of absolute automorphisms of X̃ compatible with some automorphism of X. This is a slip, not a mathematical error.
X̃ must be understood as the universal pro-étale covering (a projective system) for (6) to be exact with π1 the profinite étale group. The page is silent on this, but it is standard for Grothendieck.

The NB as transcribed ('Si 𝒢_X est fini, 𝒢_X est profini') is tautological. It should read 'if G_X = Aut(X/Q̄) is finite'. Openness of the stabiliser also tacitly uses that 𝒢_X → Γ has open image (finite type case, p.1).

ideas.what: Exact sequence 1 → π1(X) → ℰ_X → 𝒢_X → 1. It extends the group of semilinear (absolute) automorphisms of X by the geometric fundamental group, and contains the usual 1 → π1(X_Q̄) → π1(X_K) → Γ_K over any field of definition K.
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental exact sequence / arithmetic fundamental group; equivalently π1 of the quotient stack [X/𝒢_X] over Q
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1 IX.6 for the homotopy exact sequence); the equivariant/stack version is folklore (Noohi, Zoonekynd on π1 of stacks)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exposé IX (fundamental exact sequence); Esquisse d'un programme (Galois action on π1 of moduli / Teichmüller tower)

ideas.what: Rational/algebraic point ξ gives a splitting of the extension over its stabiliser, unique up to π1-conjugation, via a pointed universal cover.
ideas.modern_name: Section associated to a rational point (the 'section map' X(K) → {sections}/π1-conjugacy)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, letter to Faltings (1983), section conjecture
ideas.where_published: Letter to G. Faltings, 27 June 1983 (published in Geometric Galois Actions 1, 1997)

ideas.what: Model-free formulation: work with X over Q̄ and its full group of absolute automorphisms rather than a model over a number field. The image of 𝒢_X → Γ corresponds to the field of moduli; germs of lifts (p.3) give fields of definition.
ideas.modern_name: Field of moduli vs field of definition; Galois descent obstruction

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up the section-map formalism (point ↦ conjugacy class of splitting) equivariantly with respect to the whole absolute automorphism group 𝒢_X, including geometric automorphisms, with no fixed field of definition. This is c. 1980–81, slightly before the 1983 Faltings letter. It is a documentary datum on the genesis of the section conjecture framework rather than a new mathematical result. The stack-theoretic version (sections of π1 of [X/G]) was later developed by others.
missed.quote: si on choisit pour X̃ le rev. universel pointé au dessus de ξ, un splitting partiel de (6)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical precursor to the section conjecture in a field-of-moduli / equivariant setting. It is of minor interest for dating the genesis of the anabelian programme.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard material: the homotopy exact sequence and the sections attached to points, here in a slightly more general absolute-automorphism form. Mildly interesting as an early (c.1980) dated draft of the section-map formalism in a moduli-free setting, but nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: In the NB, the hypothesis is most likely 'Si G_X [geometric automorphism group] est fini, 𝒢_X est profini et 𝒢_X(ξ) est un ss-groupe ouvert', not '𝒢_X fini'.
Interlinear note under 'le sous-groupe' reads roughly 'X est de t.f. / Q̄' or 'X est déf. / Q̄ … r'. It is a marginal hypothesis (finite type over Q̄) needed for openness.
(8) is a triangle: ℰ_X → 𝒢_X → 1, with 𝒢_X(ξ) ↪ 𝒢_X and a diagonal arrow 𝒢_X(ξ) → ℰ_X.
The superscript added near 'rev. universel' is 'X̃(ξ)' (the pointed universal covering), inserted above 'pointé'.
'on en trouve qu'un hom.' should read 'on ne trouve qu'un hom. mod composition avec automorphismes intérieurs provenant de π1(X)'.
